mainTopic: How much extra load makes one liable; the משנה on paid and unpaid guardians (craftsmen, guarding swaps, lenders); whether it fits רבי מאיר; and a borrower's liability after the loan period.
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a question. A ברייתא about a donkey seems to contradict the rule that adding three קבין makes the renter liable, and אביי answers that the ברייתא is talking about leveled measures. A second ברייתא lists how much extra load is too much for a porter and for boats of several sizes. אביי, רבא and רב אשי each explain why a porter does not just throw off a load that is too heavy. רב פפא learns from the same ברייתא that an ordinary ship holds thirty כור, which matters for buying and selling. A new משנה then lists who counts as a שומר שכר and who counts as a שומר חנם: craftsmen, people who swap guarding, and lenders holding a משכון. The גמרא asks whether the craftsman ruling goes against רבי מאיר and tries several reasons to fit them together, and it also offers רבה בר אבוה's reversed version of the ברייתא. Finally רב חסדא limits a borrower's liability to the loan period, and רב נחמן בר פפא begins a challenge from our משנה that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to exempt an extra three קבין
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא makes the renter liable only at sixteen סאה of barley, which implies that adding three קבין is exempt. That clashes with the three-קבין rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says that if he loaded sixteen סאה of barley, he is liable. That implies that if he added only three קבין, he is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads a ברייתא and points out what it implies. It sets that implication against the rule that adding three קבין already makes the renter liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names a whole extra סאה (six קבין) as the point of liability. So a smaller addition, like three קבין, would seem to be exempt. That contradicts the rule that three קבין is already enough to make him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt, does not have to pay
קבין, a small dry measure (six קבין make one סאה)

steps.confusionAlert: This section starts in the middle of a question. The first words are the end of a ברייתא, and the challenge comes from what it implies.

phrases.english: Sixteen [se'a of] barley – he is liable.
This implies that with three kav [added] – he is exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of how much extra load makes the renter liable.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that sets liability at sixteen סאה of barley.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies that a smaller addition, such as three קבין, is exempt. That contradicts the rule that three קבין already makes him liable.

steps.title: אביי: the ברייתא is talking about leveled measures
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ברייתא measures level, not heaped, so its numbers do not really clash with the three-קבין rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי explained the ברייתא: it is talking about leveled measures.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction by explaining how the grain in the ברייתא was measured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain is usually measured heaped up above the rim of the measure. The ברייתא is talking about measures smoothed flat, so each of its סאה is smaller than an ordinary one. Its sixteen סאה therefore does not really mean a larger extra amount than the three-קבין rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it, he interpreted the source

phrases.english: Abaye interpreted it: [it refers] to smoothed-over [measures].
phrases.notes: Smoothed-over means the grain was leveled off at the rim instead of piled up on top.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to a specific way of measuring.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא uses ordinary heaped סאה, so it requires a much bigger addition than three קבין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא uses leveled measures, so there is no real contradiction.

steps.title: A ברייתא: how much extra is too much for a porter and for boats
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the extra load that counts as too much for a porter, a small boat, a regular ship and a large ship.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a קב is too much extra for a porter, an אדריב for a small boat, a כור for a ship, and three כור for a large ship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that gives the limit of extra load for several kinds of carriers. The next steps will discuss it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about the donkey is extended to other carriers. Each carrier has its own amount of extra weight that counts as an overload. If someone adds that much and harm results, he is responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: A porter who carries loads on his shoulders

phrases.english: The Sages taught: A kav for a porter,
phrases.notes: Each item is the amount of extra load that counts as too much for that carrier.

phrases.english: An adriv for a small boat.
A kor for a boat,
Three kor for a large ship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא that extends the overload limits to other carriers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An extra קב overloads a porter, an אדריב a small boat, a כור a ship, and three כור a large ship.

steps.title: Why doesn't the porter just throw it off?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the porter needs a ruling at all. If the load is too heavy, a sensible person would throw it down.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said: a קב is too much for a porter. But if he really can't carry it, he is a sensible person, so let him throw it off!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first line of the ברייתא and challenges it. The porter can feel the weight himself, so why would he be hurt?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A donkey cannot speak up for itself, but a porter is a thinking person. If the extra weight is too much, he should drop it and avoid getting hurt. So why would the person who loaded him be responsible, or why is this rule needed at all?

phrases.english: The Master said: A kav for a porter.
If it is so that he cannot [bear] it,
he is a sensible person; let him throw it off!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אִיתָא דְּלָא מָצֵי בֵּיהּ בַּר דַּעַת הוּא, לִשְׁדְּיֵהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first line of the ברייתא in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that an extra קב counts as an overload for a porter.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A porter can sense the weight and drop it himself, so the rule seems unnecessary.

steps.title: אביי: the load knocked him down right away
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the case is where the load knocked the porter down at once, before he could throw it off.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it is where the load knocked him down immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first answer. The porter had no chance to throw off the load.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being sensible only helps if there is time to react. Here the extra weight struck him down immediately, so he could not protect himself.

keyTerms.meaning: It knocked him down, it struck him

phrases.english: Abaye said: Where it knocked him down immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to a specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The porter always had time to throw off the load.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about a case where he had no time, because the load knocked him down at once.

steps.title: רבא: the rule is about extra pay
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even if the porter was not knocked down, the ברייתא teaches that a קב is enough of an addition for him to demand extra wages.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: even if you say it did not knock him down immediately, the rule is needed only for extra pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. The ברייתא is not about injury at all but about the porter's wages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא agrees that a sensible porter would throw off a load that is dangerous. So for him the ברייתא is about money: an extra קב is a real addition, and the porter may demand more pay for carrying it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for, the rule is only teaching

phrases.english: Rava said: Even if you say
where it did not knock him down immediately,
it is necessary only for extra pay.
phrases.notes: In other words, an extra קב is enough for the porter to ask for higher wages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 4, different from אביי's in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes what the ruling is about, from injury to wages.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about paying for an injury.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא teaches that an extra קב entitles the porter to extra pay.

steps.title: רב אשי: he thought he was just feeling weak
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the porter did not drop the load because he blamed his own weakness, not the extra weight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: he thought it was a weakness that had seized him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third answer. The porter did not realize that the load was the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being sensible does not help if you misread the situation. The porter felt the strain but assumed he was just tired or weak for the moment. So he kept carrying and got hurt, and the one who overloaded him is responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: Has taken hold of him, seized him

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: He thought
it was weakness that seized him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הוּא סָבוּר חוּלְשָׁא הוּא דְּנָקֵיט לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer to step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why a sensible person still would not throw off the load.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A sensible porter would always recognize the overload.
steps.terutzMaskana: He blamed his own weakness and did not realize the load was too heavy.
steps.whatToRemember: Three answers to 'why doesn't the porter throw it off?': אביי, he had no time; רבא, the rule is about extra pay; רב אשי, he thought the problem was his own weakness.

steps.title: רב פפא: an ordinary ship holds thirty כור
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא quotes the ships line of the ברייתא and learns from it that an ordinary ship carries thirty כור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: a כור for a ship, three כור for a large ship. רב פפא said: learn from this that ordinary ships hold thirty כור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ships line of the ברייתא again, this time so that רב פפא can draw a new conclusion from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Throughout these rules, the overload is one-thirtieth of the normal load. So if one כור is too much extra for a ship, a normal ship must carry thirty כור. רב פפא uses the ברייתא to learn the standard size of a ship.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary ships, ships whose size was not specified

phrases.english: A kor for a boat,
three kor for a large ship.
Rav Pappa said: Learn from this
that unspecified boats hold thirty kor.
phrases.notes: The extra amount that counts as too much is always one-thirtieth of the normal load, so one כור points to thirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ships line of the ברייתא in step 3 to learn something new from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ordinary ship carries thirty כור.

steps.title: What difference does a ship's size make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference it makes to know the standard size of a ship.
steps.simpleTranslation: What practical difference does this make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב פפא's observation matters. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing that an ordinary ship holds thirty כור sounds like a simple fact. The גמרא wants to know what law depends on it.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the practical use of רב פפא's statement in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What law depends on knowing the standard size of a ship.

steps.title: It matters for buying and selling
steps.stepSummary: The answer: when someone sells a ship without saying its size, the buyer can expect one that holds thirty כור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It matters for buying and selling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the standard size matters in sales.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone sells 'a ship' without saying how big it is, the standard size decides what the buyer is owed. He can expect a ship that holds thirty כור.
steps.whatToRemember: From the overload amounts, רב פפא learns that an ordinary ship holds thirty כור, and this matters when a ship is sold without stating its size.

phrases.english: For buying and selling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The standard size of thirty כור sets what a buyer can expect when a ship is sold without stating its size.

steps.title: Craftsmen are paid guardians until they say 'take it and pay'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that all craftsmen are שומרי שכר over the items they work on. Once a craftsman says 'take your item and bring money', he becomes a שומר חנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All craftsmen are paid guardians. But any of them who said, 'Take what is yours and bring the money,' is only an unpaid guardian.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says a craftsman holding your item is a paid guardian, but once he finishes and tells you to come get it, he drops to an unpaid guardian.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the craftsman holds the item to earn his wage, he is a שומר שכר and is liable even for theft or loss. Once the job is done and he says 'take it and pay me', he is no longer holding it to earn anything. So he is only a שומר חנם, liable just for carelessness.

keyTerms.meaning: Craftsmen or skilled workers who take items to work on them
Paid guardian; liable even for theft and loss
Unpaid guardian; liable only for carelessness

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל הָאוּמָּנִין – שׁוֹמְרֵי שָׂכָר הֵן.
phrases.english: MISHNA: All craftsmen are paid guardians.
And all of them who said:
"Take what is yours and bring money"
are an unpaid guardian.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of the porter and the ship.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A craftsman is a שומר שכר. After he says 'take yours and bring money', he is a שומר חנם.

steps.title: Guarding for each other versus 'put it in front of me'
steps.stepSummary: If two people agree to guard for each other, each is a שומר שכר. If one asks the other to guard and the other just says 'put it down in front of me', he is only a שומר חנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one says, 'Guard mine and I'll guard yours,' each is a paid guardian. If one says, 'Guard this for me,' and the other answers, 'Put it down in front of me,' he is an unpaid guardian.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two more cases. A swap of guarding counts as payment, but a casual 'leave it here' does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the swap, each person's 'payment' is that the other guards his things, so each is a שומר שכר. In the second case, 'put it in front of me' gets the guardian nothing in return. It also sounds like he is not really taking on the job, so he is at most a שומר חנם.

keyTerms.meaning: Guard for me and I'll guard for you: a guarding swap
Put it down in front of me

phrases.english: "Guard for me and I will guard for you"
is a paid guardian.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמוֹר לִי, וְאָמַר לוֹ: הַנַּח לְפָנַי –
phrases.english: "Guard for me," and he said to him: "Put it down in front of me"
is an unpaid guardian.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of guardian categories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A guarding swap makes each person a שומר שכר. 'Put it before me' makes him a שומר חנם.

steps.title: A lender holding collateral, and רבי יהודה's split
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says a lender holding a משכון is a שומר שכר. רבי יהודה splits it: lending money makes him a שומר חנם, lending produce makes him a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone lent another person money and took collateral, he is a paid guardian over it. רבי יהודה says: if he lent money, he is an unpaid guardian; if he lent produce, he is a paid guardian.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to a lender who holds a pledge. The first opinion makes him a paid guardian, and רבי יהודה disagrees in part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא sees the lender as gaining something from holding the משכון, so he is a שומר שכר. רבי יהודה only gives him that status when he lent produce. The משנה does not explain why here.

keyTerms.meaning: Collateral or pledge given for a loan

phrases.english: If he lent him on collateral, he is a paid guardian.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
If he lent him money, he is an unpaid guardian;
if he lent him produce, he is a paid guardian.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the case of a lender holding a משכון, with a disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: a lender holding a משכון is a שומר שכר. רבי יהודה: money loan makes him a שומר חנם, produce loan makes him a שומר שכר.

steps.title: Renting out a poor man's collateral
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול allows a lender to rent out a poor borrower's משכון and take the rent off the debt, since this is like השבת אבידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: a person may rent out a poor man's collateral and keep lowering the debt with the rent money, because this is like returning a lost item.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with אבא שאול's ruling. A lender may earn rent from a poor borrower's pledge as long as the rent goes toward paying off the loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually you may not use a borrower's pledge. אבא שאול permits it here because the poor man gains: his debt shrinks instead of the item just sitting unused. Helping him this way is compared to returning a lost object.

keyTerms.meaning: Setting a price and steadily reducing the debt

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lists who is a שומר שכר: craftsmen, people who swap guarding, and a lender holding a משכון (with רבי יהודה's split). It also lists who is a שומר חנם: a craftsman after 'take yours', and someone who says 'put it before me'.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
A person is permitted to rent out
the collateral of a poor man
setting a price on it and steadily reducing the debt,
because he is like one who returns a lost item.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: רַשַּׁאי אָדָם לְהַשְׂכִּיר מַשְׁכּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related rule about using a poor man's משכון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may rent out a poor borrower's משכון and take the rent off the debt.

steps.title: Does the משנה go against רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה does not follow רבי מאיר. A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר says a שוכר pays like a שומר חנם, while the משנה makes the craftsman a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Shall we say our משנה does not follow רבי מאיר? For a ברייתא teaches: How does a renter pay? רבי מאיר says: like an unpaid guardian. רבי יהודה says: like a paid guardian.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא worries that the משנה's ruling on craftsmen clashes with רבי מאיר. It brings a ברייתא about a renter as evidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A craftsman, like a renter, holds someone else's item to benefit from it. רבי מאיר says such a person (a שוכר) is only a שומר חנם. Yet the משנה makes craftsmen שומרי שכר, so it seems to fit רבי יהודה and not רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא may reject)
Renter: one who rents an item

steps.confusionAlert: שׂוֹכֵר here means a renter, someone who rents and uses the item. Don't mix it up with שׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר, a guardian who gets paid. The words look alike but are different roles.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר?
phrases.english: GEMARA: Shall we say our Mishna is not like Rabbi Meir?
For it is taught in a baraita:
A renter, how does he pay?
Rabbi Meir says: like an unpaid guardian.
Rabbi Yehuda says: like a paid guardian.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's first ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that craftsmen are שומרי שכר (step 11).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A craftsman is like a שוכר. רבי מאיר makes a שוכר only a שומר חנם, so the משנה seems to go against רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Craftsman gains by being chosen
steps.stepSummary: The משנה can fit רבי מאיר. A craftsman becomes a שומר שכר because of the benefit he gets when the owner picks him over everyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי מאיר. Because of the benefit he gets when the owner passes over everyone else and hires him, he becomes a paid guardian over the item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר could agree with the משנה. The craftsman has a special reason to be a paid guardian.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The craftsman's 'payment' for guarding is not the item itself. It is the business he got because the owner chose him. That benefit is enough to make him a שומר שכר even according to רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: You can even say it is Rabbi Meir:
through that benefit
that he passes over everyone else
phrases.notes: 'He' here is the owner, who skips all the other craftsmen.

phrases.english: and hires him specifically,
he becomes a paid guardian over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a separate reason why the craftsman is a paid guardian, one that does not depend on the שוכר debate.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's ruling on craftsmen contradicts רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי מאיר agrees a craftsman is a שומר שכר, because he benefits from being chosen over others.

steps.title: A renter is also chosen over everyone else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: by that reasoning, a שוכר also benefits when the owner rents to him over everyone else, so רבי מאיר should make him a שומר שכר too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a renter too: because of the benefit he gets when the owner passes over everyone else and rents to him, he should become a paid guardian over the item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. The same logic would apply to a renter, yet רבי מאיר makes a renter only an unpaid guardian. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being chosen makes someone a שומר שכר, a renter is chosen too. Then רבי מאיר's ruling that a renter pays like a שומר חנם makes no sense. So the answer in step 16 cannot be complete as it stands, and the גמרא will need to explain what makes the craftsman different.

phrases.english: If so, a renter too:
through that benefit
that he passes over everyone else
and rents it out to him specifically,
he should become a paid guardian over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning in step 16 that the benefit of being chosen makes one a שומר שכר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A renter gets the same benefit of being chosen. Yet רבי מאיר rules a renter is a שומר חנם, so being chosen cannot be enough.

steps.title: A new reason: the craftsman is paid a little extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the earlier reason and says the craftsman is a שומר שכר because the owner usually pays him a bit more than the exact wage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you can even say the משנה follows רבי מאיר. Because of the benefit that the owner gives the craftsman a little extra, the craftsman becomes a שומר שכר over the item.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier reason was knocked down in step 17. So the גמרא offers a different reason why the craftsman is a שומר שכר even according to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old reason was that the owner picked this craftsman over everyone else, but that would apply to a שוכר too. The new reason points to money: a craftsman's wage is hard to measure exactly, so he usually gets paid a little more than he earned. That extra payment is the benefit that makes him a שומר שכר.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Signals that the previous answer is dropped and a new one is coming
You can even say. The answer works even according to this opinion

phrases.english: Rather: you can even say it follows רבי מאיר,
through that benefit, that the owner gives him
a little more,
phrases.notes: A craftsman's exact wage is hard to pin down, so the owner usually pays him a bit extra.

phrases.english: he becomes a paid guardian over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that was rejected in step 17 with a new reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reasoning for the same conclusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The craftsman's benefit was being chosen over others, which also applies to a שוכר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The craftsman's benefit is the slight overpayment he receives, which makes him a שומר שכר.

steps.title: A renter also gets a little extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a שוכר also often gets slightly more value than he pays for, so the new reason should make him a שומר שכר too.
steps.simpleTranslation: A renter too! Aren't we dealing even with a case where the owner gives him a little extra value? Yet רבי מאיר still calls him a שומר חנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new answer from step 18. A renter can also get a little extra, so that cannot be what makes the craftsman different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If getting 'a little more' makes someone a שומר שכר, then a שוכר who gets a good deal should be one too. But in the ברייתא, רבי מאיר says a שוכר pays only like a שומר חנם. So the 'little extra' reason does not explain the difference between them.

keyTerms.meaning: A renter, someone who pays to use another person's item
Aren't we dealing with... A way of saying the case clearly includes this situation

phrases.english: A renter too!
Are we not dealing
with a case where the owner gives him a little more value?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason given in step 18, that slight overpayment makes the craftsman a שומר שכר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שוכר also often gets slightly more value than he pays, yet רבי מאיר treats him as a שומר חנם. So the reason does not separate the two cases.

steps.title: The craftsman can hold the item until he is paid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a third reason: the craftsman benefits because he can keep the item until he is paid, so he never has to chase after his money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you can even say the משנה follows רבי מאיר. Because of the benefit that he holds onto the item for his wage, so he doesn't have to keep going in and out to collect his money, he becomes a שומר שכר over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the 'little extra' reason and gives a new one. The craftsman holds the item like a guarantee for his pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This benefit belongs only to the craftsman. A renter has nothing to collect, but a craftsman is owed wages and can keep the item until he gets them. That security is real value to him, so even רבי מאיר would make him a שומר שכר.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds onto, keeps in his hands
To go in and go out, meaning to keep going back and forth

steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, the craftsman is a שומר שכר even according to רבי מאיר because he keeps the item as security for his wages, a benefit a renter does not have.

phrases.english: Rather, you can even say it follows רבי מאיר,
through that benefit, that he holds onto it for his wage,
so that he does not need to go in and go out for his money,
he becomes a paid guardian over it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, בְּהַהִיא הֲנָאָה דְּתָפֵישׂ לֵיהּ אַאַגְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 with a reason that applies only to a craftsman.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reasoning that applies only to the craftsman
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The craftsman's benefit was a slight overpayment, which a renter also gets.
steps.terutzMaskana: The craftsman's benefit is holding the item as security for his pay, which a renter does not have.

steps.title: Another answer: רבה בר אבוה's reversed version of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: As another option, the גמרא brings רבה בר אבוה's version of the ברייתא, which switches the opinions so that רבי מאיר says a שוכר pays like a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say instead what רבה בר אבוה teaches, with the opinions switched: How does a renter pay? רבי מאיר says like a שומר שכר. רבי יהודה says like a שומר חנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a completely different way to fit the משנה with רבי מאיר. It reads the ברייתא with the two opinions switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original problem in step 15 was that רבי מאיר treats a שוכר like a שומר חנם. In רבה בר אבוה's version, רבי מאיר treats a שוכר like a שומר שכר. Then there is no conflict at all with the משנה making a craftsman a שומר שכר, and no special reason is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say... Introduces another possible answer

steps.confusionAlert: Be careful not to mix up the two versions. In the first version (step 15) רבי מאיר says a שוכר is like a שומר חנם. In רבה בר אבוה's version רבי מאיר says a שוכר is like a שומר שכר.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
as רבה בר אבוה switches the opinions and teaches:
A renter, how does he pay?
רבי מאיר says: like a paid guardian;
רבי יהודה says: like an unpaid guardian.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, כִּדְמַחְלֵיף רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ וְתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to the question of step 15, alongside the answer in step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In the ברייתא, רבי מאיר says a שוכר pays like a שומר חנם, which seems to clash with the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: In רבה בר אבוה's version, רבי מאיר says a שוכר pays like a שומר שכר, so the משנה fits רבי מאיר easily.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: 'Take yours and bring money'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: anyone who told the owner 'take your item and bring the money' is only a שומר חנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all those who said, 'Take what is yours and bring money,' are unpaid guardians.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the craftsman tells the owner 'take your item and bring the money,' he no longer holds it as security for his pay. He is only watching it as a favor, so he is just a שומר חנם.

keyTerms.meaning: And all those who said, meaning all the guardians listed in the משנה

phrases.english: And all those who said:
"Take what is yours and bring money,"
is an unpaid guardian.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלָּן שֶׁאָמְרוּ: טוֹל אֶת שֶׁלְּךָ וְהָבֵא מָעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A guardian who told the owner 'take your item and bring the money' is only a שומר חנם.

steps.title: A related משנה about a borrower who says 'send it'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another משנה: if a borrower told the lender to send the animal and it died on the way, the borrower is liable, and the same applies when he returns it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: If the borrower told the lender 'send it,' and he sent it and it died, the borrower is liable. The same is true when he returns it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from another place. It is setting up a discussion that will connect to the line it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the borrower says 'send it,' he takes on responsibility for the animal even while it is on the way to him. The משנה adds that the same is true on the way back, and the גמרא will now examine what that means.

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This משנה appears later in this same מסכת (צח:).

phrases.english: If the borrower said to him, "Send it,"
and he sent it and it died, he is liable;
and the same applies when he returns it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: אָמַר לוֹ שׁוֹאֵל שַׁלַּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside משנה to start the discussion of the line quoted in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A borrower who said 'send it' is liable if the animal dies on the way, and likewise when he returns it.

steps.title: The borrower is only liable if he returned the animal during the loan period
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא limits the משנה about returning a borrowed animal. The borrower is liable only if he returned it during the loan period. After the loan period he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם בר פפא said in the name of רב חסדא: The משנה only taught this ruling when the borrower returned the animal during the time of its loan. But if he returned it after the time of its loan, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא narrows the משנה from the previous step. The borrower is responsible for an animal that dies on the way back only if he sends it back before the loan period ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the loan period is running, the borrower has the full responsibility of a שואל, so a death on the way is his problem. Once the agreed loan time is over, he no longer counts as a borrower. So רב חסדא says he is פטור if the animal dies on the way.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught this when...': a formula that limits a ruling to a specific case
The days of its loan, meaning the agreed time the animal was borrowed for
A borrower, who carries the heaviest level of responsibility

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying the borrower is never responsible. רב חסדא only says that once the loan time is over, he is no longer under a borrower's special liability.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rafram bar Pappa said that Rav Ḥisda said:
They taught this only
when he returned it within the days of its loan.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the borrowed animal from the משנה in the previous step, which died on the way back.

phrases.english: But after the days of its loan, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה quoted in step 23 to a borrower who returns the animal during the loan period.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A borrower who sends back the animal is liable for its death on the way only if the loan period had not yet ended. After the loan period, he is exempt.

steps.title: A challenge from the line about 'take your item and bring money'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר פפא begins an objection to רב חסדא by quoting our משנה: someone who said 'take your item and bring money' is a שומר חנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר פפא raised an objection: And all those who said, 'Take what is yours and bring money,' are each an unpaid guardian.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר פפא is setting up a challenge against רב חסדא. He quotes the line of our משנה that the גמרא brought in step 22. The explanation of the challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that line of the משנה, a person's main role is finished, yet he still carries the responsibility of a שומר חנם. He is not completely free. This seems to clash with רב חסדא's claim that a borrower is simply פטור once the loan period ends. The גמרא spells out the clash on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Take your item and bring money': the case in the משנה where the job is done and the worker tells the owner to come pay and collect
An unpaid guardian, liable only for negligence

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Pappa raises an objection:
And all those who said,
'Take what is yours and bring money,'
phrases.notes: This is the line of our משנה that was quoted back in step 22.

phrases.english: are an unpaid guardian.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against רב חסדא's ruling in step 24, using the line of the משנה from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that a borrower is exempt once the loan period has ended
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה shows that a person whose main obligation has ended still keeps the duty of a שומר חנם. That seems to contradict a complete exemption after the loan period. The detailed reasoning follows in the next lines of the גמרא.
